CODE 
Art. 2.3.66. 
Composition of the original patrimony 
The original patrimony is the patrimony of each of the spouses on the date on which the matrimonial property regime takes effect. Debts are taken into account in the original patrimony, even when they exceed the amount of the assets.
Property and rights acquired subsequently by each of the spouses by gift or inheritance, as well as those referred to in Article 2.3.19, ¤ 1, 1¡, and ¤ 2, are added to the original patrimony. The debts referred to in Articles 2.3.23 and 2.3.24 are taken into account in the original patrimony, even where they exceed the amount of the assets.   
The original patrimony does not include: 
1¡ the fruits of the property of which it is composed; 
2¡ property of the original patrimony given by a spouse to relatives in the direct line during the matrimonial regime.
At the time of the conclusion of the matrimonial agreement, the spouses draw up an inventory of their respective original assets. This inventory is presumed to be accurate when both spouses have signed it.
If no inventory has been drawn up, the original patrimony is presumed to be null.
